entities.summary: Joseph Heinrich Beuys was a German artist, teacher, performance artist, and art theorist whose work reflected concepts of humanism and sociology. With Heinrich Böll, Johannes Stüttgen, Caroline Tisdall, Robert McDowell, and Enrico Wolleb, Beuys created the Free International University for Creativity & Interdisciplinary Research (FIU). Through his talks and performances, he also formed The Party for Animals and The Organisation for Direct Democracy. He was a member of a Dadaist art movement Fluxus and singularly inspirational in developing of Performance Art, called Kunst Aktionen, alongside Wiener Aktionismus that Allan Kaprow and Carolee Schneemann termed Art Happenings.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Joseph Beuys' work in Performance Art and Kunst Aktionen influenced the development of Fluxus and Wiener Aktionismus, contributing to the emergence of Art Happenings. His involvement with The Party for Animals and The Organisation for Direct Democracy reflects his commitment to social activism.
